summary: A 1942 cabin lookout on Medicine Butte near Reliance, Lyman County, was planned for round-the-clock watch; the cabin is gone.

facts.design: Small cabin on the butte top

events.note: Round-the-clock watch planned, per a July 1942 Daily Republic item quoted by Forest Lookouts.

evidence.quote: has been selected as a lookout station

evidence.supports: six miles north of Reliance, Lyman County
view covers Lyman County and parts of five counties
evidence.quote: which overlooks all of Lyman county and parts of Stanley, Hughes, Hyde, Brule and Buffalo
Plans are being made to have someone on this lookout with binoculars 24 hours a day.

evidence.supports: telephone line by local farmers; road to the shack
evidence.quote: A telephone line to the top of the Butte is being constructed by the local farmers and a road has already been built to the shack on top of the Butte.

evidence.supports: filed under Lyman County and the state
near Reliance; about 200 feet above prairie; sacred to Brule Sioux people
evidence.quote: Medicine Butte is near Reliance. It rises about 200 feet above the prairie, and is sacred to the Brulé Sioux people, especially those who live on the nearby Lower Brule Indian Reservation

notes_for_editor: Only two pages describe the site in detail. The 1942 newspaper item reaches us through Forest Lookouts, which quotes The Daily Republic; the Daily Republic itself was not read. Firelookout.com's 'Co-op' label is unexplained and was not used. The Wikipedia article titled Medicine Butte is about a Wyoming butte, not this one, and was not used. The 1942 item already describes a shack on top, so the 1942 build date from firelookout.com is only a date for the cabin, not confirmed by a construction record. No source gives the date the cabin came down or the summit's condition now. Brief's status (gone), kind (ground) and agency (State) are supported; no correction proposed.
